mainTopic: The sprinklings toward the כפורת on יום הכיפורים: where the blood goes, how many sprinklings there are, how they are counted, and רבי יהודה's concern about mix-ups
overview: This amud explains how the כהן גדול sprinkles blood toward the כפורת on יום הכיפורים. A ברייתא teaches that the blood is aimed at the front edge of the כפורת, not onto its top. רבי זירא finds the source in an extra phrase about the שעיר, which shows that 'על' means 'not actually on.' The גמרא tries to reverse this with אדרבה, but rejects the reversal, because it would leave a phrase in the verse with no purpose. Next, a ברייתא works out that both the פר and the שעיר get one upward and seven downward sprinklings. After several competing comparisons, the extra words 'כאשר עשה' settle it. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה give two styles of counting the sprinklings, and the גמרא says each simply followed his local custom. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן give different reasons why the first sprinkling is counted with every later one. Finally, the גמרא turns to the golden stand and to רבי יהודה's worry about mix-ups in the bird-offering boxes, and the answer to אביי's challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the whip image
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the previous description: the כהן גדול moves his hand like someone swinging a whip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like one who lashes with a whip.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word closes the description from the previous page. The כהן גדול's sprinkling motion is compared to a man swinging a whip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone whipping another person's back hits one spot, then the next strike lands a little lower, then lower again. The comparison shows that the sprinklings come one after another in a line going down. This sets up the ברייתא that follows, which describes the hand motion in more detail.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sprinkling motion is like the strokes of a whip, each one falling a bit lower than the last.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the blood is aimed at the front edge of the כפורת, not on top of it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the כהן גדול does not sprinkle onto the כפורת itself. He aims at its front thickness and turns his hand differently for upward and downward sprinklings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When he sprinkles, he does not sprinkle on the כפורת. He sprinkles facing the thickness of the כפורת. When he sprinkles upward, he turns his hand downward. When he sprinkles downward, he turns his hand upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that describes exactly where the blood goes. The blood is aimed at the front edge of the כפורת, not onto its top surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כפורת is a thick slab of gold, so it has a front edge. The ברייתא says the כהן גדול aims at that edge and never sprinkles on the top. For the one upward sprinkling he turns the back of his hand downward, and for the seven downward sprinklings he turns it upward, much like the motion of a whip.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The golden cover on top of the ארון
Its thickness (the front edge)
He turns his hand to the side / tilts his hand
Upward / downward

steps.confusionAlert: 'Upward' and 'downward' describe the direction of the sprinkling (one upward and seven downward). They do not mean sprinkling on top of the כפורת or under it. According to this ברייתא, the blood never lands on the top surface of the כפורת.

steps.title: What is the source that the blood does not land on the כפורת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא learns that the blood does not actually go on the כפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the ברייתא's rule. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'על הכפורת,' which sounds like 'on the כפורת.' So the גמרא wants to know how the ברייתא can say the blood does not go on it. The answer has to explain this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the ברייתא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse showing that the sprinklings do not actually touch the כפורת, even though the פסוק says 'על הכפורת.'

steps.title: רבי זירא: the downward sprinkling of the שעיר did not need to be written
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא points out that the verse about the שעיר mentions 'לפני הכפורת' (the downward sprinklings) even though this could already be learned from the פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said in the name of רבי זירא: The verse says, 'And he shall sprinkle it upon the כפורת and before the כפורת.' The Torah did not need to say 'downward' by the שעיר, because that is already learned from the downward sprinklings of the פר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins his answer by noticing that some words in the verse about the שעיר are extra. He is setting up a lesson that will come from those extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the שעיר's blood is done 'just like the blood of the פר,' so every detail of the פר already applies to the שעיר. That makes 'לפני הכפורת' (the downward sprinklings) by the שעיר unnecessary. When the Torah repeats something it did not need to say, it is teaching something new.

Since it is not needed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the source question by identifying extra wording in the verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'לפני הכפורת' by the שעיר is extra, since the שעיר's procedure is already learned from the פר. It is therefore available to teach something new.

steps.title: The היקש: 'upon' is like 'before', so it does not actually touch
steps.stepSummary: The extra words link 'על' to 'לפני'. Just as 'before' means not on the כפורת, 'upon' also means not actually on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why was it written? To compare 'upon' to 'before.' Just as 'before' means not on the כפורת, so too 'upon' means not on the כפורת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finishes his answer. The extra words create a היקש showing that 'על הכפורת' does not really mean the blood lands on the כפורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפני' (in front of) clearly means not touching the top. Because the Torah put the two words side by side for no other reason, 'על' takes on the same meaning. This is the source for the ברייתא's rule that the blood is only aimed at the front of the כפורת.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare (make a היקש between two things)
A comparison created because the Torah places two things together
That is not on

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי זירא, the extra 'לפני' by the שעיר teaches that even 'על הכפורת' means the blood does not actually touch the top of the כפורת.

phrases.english: why was it stated?
To compare "upon" to "before":
just as "before" means not on it,
so too "upon" means not on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי זירא's derivation by explaining what the extra words teach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש makes 'על' like 'לפני': neither one means the blood actually lands on the כפורת.

steps.title: On the contrary: maybe the extra words teach that 'before' means actually on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses רבי זירא's argument. Maybe the extra wording is the upward sprinkling of the פר, and the היקש teaches that 'לפני' means actually touching the כפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The Torah did not need to say 'upward' by the פר, because that can be learned from the upward sprinkling of the שעיר. So why was it written? To compare 'before' to 'upon.' Just as 'upon' means truly on it, so too 'before' means truly on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא by flipping his logic. If we call a different phrase the 'extra' one, the היקש points the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning can go in both directions between the פר and the שעיר, so the upward sprinkling of the פר could just as well be the extra phrase. Then 'לפני' would be compared to 'על,' and since 'על' plainly means 'on,' every sprinkling would actually touch the כפורת (its thickness). The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary (introduces a reversed argument)
Actually on it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. The גמרא is only showing that רבי זירא's method could prove the opposite. Step 7 answers this challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an 'extra words' argument only works if we can explain why one specific phrase, and not another, is the extra one.

phrases.english: On the contrary:
it should not have said "upward" regarding the bull,
since it is not needed,
since it is learned from the upward sprinkling of the goat.
Why was it stated?
To compare "before" to "upon":
just as "upon" means actually on it,
so too "before" means actually on it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's היקש by reversing which phrase is extra and which direction the comparison goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's derivation that 'על' means not actually on the כפורת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the פר and the שעיר learn from each other, the extra phrase could be the upward sprinkling of the פר instead. Then 'לפני' would be compared to 'על,' which would mean the blood actually touches the כפורת, contradicting the ברייתא.

steps.title: The reversed reading fails because the bull's words are already used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reversal from Step 6. The words about the פר's upward sprinkling are needed for the lesson of דבי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, that 'פני' means the east side. The goat's 'לפני הכפורת' has no other job, so it must be the extra wording that creates the היקש. רבי זירא's reading stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of argument is this?! Say the goat's 'before' wording is the one used to compare to the bull's 'upon' wording. Then the bull's wording is still needed for its own lesson: 'פני' always means the east side. But say the bull's 'upon' wording is the one used for the comparison. Then what is the goat's 'before' wording there for? It would have no purpose at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge from Step 6. It shows that the reversed reading would leave a phrase in the verse with no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase in the Torah must teach something. In רבי זירא's reading, both phrases have a job. The goat's 'before' creates the היקש, and the bull's 'upon the face' teaches that פני means east. In the reversed reading, the goat's 'before' wording has no job left, so that reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is this?!' A sharp phrase rejecting a suggestion
'Granted, if you say…' This sets up one reading that works, before showing the other one fails
A model rule. One verse sets a pattern that applies everywhere in the Torah
East (the eastern side)
'What does it come for?' Asking what purpose a phrase would serve

steps.whatToRemember: The 'no wasted words' test decides the issue. Only the goat's 'לפני הכפורת' is truly extra, so it creates the היקש. Therefore 'על' means aiming toward the כפורת, not touching it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'על פני הכפורת קדמה' is about the פר, and it is busy teaching that פני means east. That is why it cannot be the 'extra' phrase. Do not mix it up with the goat's 'לפני הכפורת.'

steps.title: A ברייתא asks how many downward sprinklings the goat gets
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא quotes the verse about the שעיר. The verse shows there is one upward sprinkling, because it says 'והזה' once. It does not say how many downward sprinklings there are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: 'And he shall sprinkle it upon the כפורת and before the כפורת.' We have learned how many upward sprinklings the goat gets: one. But for the downward sprinklings of the goat, I do not know how many there are!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that raises an open question: how many downward sprinklings does the שעיר get? This sets up the derivations in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the פר, the verse states 'seven' for the downward sprinklings. For the שעיר, the verse gives no number for the downward sprinklings. The ברייתא must find the number from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא
'And he shall sprinkle'
Upward / downward sprinklings
'I do not know how many'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

'and before the Ark cover'
We have learned:
how many upward sprinklings for the goat: one.
For the downward sprinklings of the goat, I do not know how many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the number of downward sprinklings for the goat
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse shows one upward sprinkling for the שעיר but gives no number for its downward sprinklings

steps.title: First answer: learn seven from the bull's downward sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares the goat to the bull. Both have downward sprinklings, and the bull's downward sprinklings are seven. So the goat's downward sprinklings are also seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will reason it out. Blood sprinkled downward is mentioned for the bull, and blood sprinkled downward is mentioned for the goat. Just as the bull's downward sprinklings are seven, so too the goat's downward sprinklings are seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests an answer. It learns the goat's downward number from the bull's downward number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals share the same kind of sprinkling (downward, in front of the כפורת). For the פר, the Torah says 'seven' outright, so the ברייתא copies that number to the שעיר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will reason it out.' This introduces a logical derivation
'Blood was mentioned' in both cases
'Just as… so too…' The comparison formula
Seven

phrases.english: I will reason it out:
blood sprinkled downward is mentioned for the bull,
and blood sprinkled downward is mentioned for the goat.
Just as the bull's downward sprinklings are seven,
so too the goat's downward sprinklings are seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many downward sprinklings the שעיר gets
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seven, learned from the downward sprinklings of the פר

steps.title: Challenge: maybe learn one from the goat's own upward sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises another option. The goat itself has one upward sprinkling, so perhaps its downward sprinklings should also be one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way instead: blood sprinkled upward is mentioned for the goat, and blood sprinkled downward is mentioned for the goat. Just as the goat's upward sprinkling is one, so too the goat's downward sprinkling should be one?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own first answer. It suggests a different comparison that gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer compared the same kind of sprinkling (downward) across two different animals. This challenge compares two kinds of sprinkling on the same animal (the שעיר). Each comparison has a reasonable claim, so the ברייתא must decide which is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or go this way.' This introduces a competing line of reasoning
One

phrases.english: Or go this way:
blood sprinkled upward is mentioned for the goat,
and blood sprinkled downward is mentioned for the goat.
Just as the goat's upward sprinkling is one,
so too the goat's downward sprinkling should be one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing comparison against Step 9's answer of seven
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of seven downward sprinklings from Step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison within the same animal (the goat's upward to the goat's downward) seems just as valid, and it gives one instead of seven

steps.title: Resolution: downward is learned from downward
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא decides between the two comparisons. Learning 'downward' from 'downward' is the closer match. So the goat gets seven downward sprinklings, like the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which case it resembles more. We learn 'downward' from 'downward.' We do not learn 'downward' from 'upward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא settles the debate by asking which comparison is the closer match. It picks the bull's downward sprinklings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The type of sprinkling matters more than which animal is being offered. Upward and downward sprinklings are different acts, so one cannot set the number for the other. This favors Step 9's answer of seven, but the next step challenges this reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us see what it resembles.' This is a test to choose the closer comparison
'We derive… from…'
Downward from downward

steps.whatToRemember: This tie-breaker (downward from downward) is only provisional. The very next step challenges it with 'גופו מגופו', and the final answer of seven rests on the verse 'כאשר עשה' (Step 13), not on this logic.

phrases.english: Let us see what it resembles:
we derive downward from downward,
and we do not derive downward from upward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between Step 9 and Step 10 in favor of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the closer comparison (same type of action)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The goat's downward sprinklings might be one, copying its own single upward sprinkling
steps.terutzMaskana: The goat's downward sprinklings are seven, learned from the bull's downward sprinklings

steps.title: On the contrary: learn the goat from itself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges the answer from Step 11. Learning the goat from the goat itself (one upward) should beat learning it from an outside animal (the bull).
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! We learn a thing from the same thing itself. We do not learn a thing from something outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own answer. It says the goat's downward sprinklings should be learned from the goat's own upward sprinkling, which is one, and not from the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said 'downward from downward' is the better match, which pointed to the bull's seven. Now a stronger rule is offered: 'גופו מגופו', learning from the same animal, beats comparing to a different animal. If that rule wins, the goat would get only one downward sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is more logical
We learn a thing from itself (from the same animal or subject)
From the outside world; from a different, unrelated subject

phrases.english: On the contrary, we derive a thing from itself,
phrases.notes: Learn the goat's downward sprinklings from the goat's own upward sprinkling, which is one.

phrases.english: and we do not derive a thing from an outside thing!
phrases.notes: Meaning: do not learn the goat from the bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the tie-breaker from Step 11 with a competing rule of comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's choice of 'downward from downward', which gives the goat seven downward sprinklings like the bull.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparing within the same animal is closer than comparing to a different animal. So the goat's own single upward sprinkling should set its downward count at one.

steps.title: The extra words 'as he did' make the goat equal to the bull
steps.stepSummary: A verse settles the question. The words 'כאשר עשה' are extra, so they teach that all of the goat's actions match the bull's. The goat therefore gets seven downward sprinklings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull.' The verse did not need to say 'as he did.' So why does it say it? To teach that all his actions should be the same. Just as the bull gets seven downward sprinklings, the goat also gets seven downward sprinklings.
steps.whatsHappening: Logic alone could not decide this, so the ברייתא brings a verse. The verse shows the goat must copy the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה already spells out the goat's sprinklings in full. So the words 'כאשר עשה' are not needed for that, and they must teach something new: the two animals are fully equal. That ends the 'גופו מגופו' argument, and the goat gets seven downward sprinklings like the bull.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; the תורה comes to say
The verse did not need to say this (so the words are extra)
'As he did', the extra phrase comparing goat to bull
All his actions are equal (identical)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'כאשר עשה' is needed to tell us how to do the goat's service. The goat's procedure is written out on its own in the verse. That is exactly why these words count as 'extra' and teach full equality.

as he did with the blood of the bull,"

phrases.notes: The goat's sprinklings are already written out in full in the same verse.

phrases.english: so why does the verse say "as he did"?
So that all his actions should be equal.

steps.title: Downward is settled, but how many upward for the bull?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up that both animals get seven downward. Then it asks a new question: how many upward sprinklings does the bull get?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned how many downward sprinklings there are: for the bull and for the goat, seven. But I do not know how many upward sprinklings there are for the bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes the downward question and opens a new one: the bull's upward count. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse for the goat clearly says one upward sprinkling (Step 8). But the verse for the bull does not give an upward number. So that is what is still missing.

steps.title: Upward from upward: the bull gets one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares the bull's upward sprinkling to the goat's upward sprinkling. The goat's is one, so the bull's is also one.
steps.simpleTranslation: I reason this way: blood sprinkled upward is mentioned for the goat, and blood sprinkled upward is mentioned for the bull. Just as the goat gets one upward, the bull also gets one upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a first answer by comparing the same kind of sprinkling (upward) across the two animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of Step 9. There the goat learned from the bull. Here the bull learns from the goat, and the goat's upward count of one is written clearly in the verse.

Blood (sprinkling) is mentioned

Just as upward with the goat is one,
so too upward with the bull is one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵינִי דָּן: נֶאֶמְרוּ דָּמִים לְמַעְלָה בַּשָּׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question from Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bull gets one upward sprinkling, learned from the goat's one upward sprinkling.

steps.title: Or learn the bull from itself: seven upward
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises another option. The bull's own downward sprinklings are seven, so maybe its upward sprinklings are also seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way instead: blood downward is mentioned for the bull, and blood upward is mentioned for the bull. Just as the bull gets seven downward, it should also get seven upward!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its first answer. It suggests comparing the bull to itself instead of to the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror of Step 10. Instead of comparing upward to upward across two animals, it compares upward to downward inside the same animal. That would give the bull seven upward sprinklings.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this other way; consider a different comparison
Seven (sprinklings)

phrases.english: Or go this way:
Blood downward is stated with the bull,
and blood upward is stated with the bull.
Just as downward with the bull is seven,
so too upward with the bull should be seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing comparison against Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's conclusion that the bull gets one upward sprinkling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bull's own downward count (seven) could just as well set its upward count, which would give seven instead of one.

steps.title: Upward is better learned from upward
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא decides that comparing upward to upward is the closer match. So the bull gets one upward sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which it is more like. We learn upward from upward. We do not learn upward from downward!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא chooses between the two comparisons. It picks the one that matches the same kind of sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing the same type of action (upward to upward) is the closer match. So the goat's one upward sprinkling sets the bull's upward count, just as in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which it resembles (choosing the closer comparison)
Upward from upward (same type of sprinkling)

phrases.english: Let us see what it resembles:
we derive upward from upward,
and we do not derive upward from downward!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by choosing the closer comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picking the better comparison, based on the same type of action.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull gets seven upward, learned from its own downward sprinklings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Upward is learned from upward, so the bull gets one upward sprinkling.

steps.title: On the contrary: learn the bull from itself
steps.stepSummary: The same objection returns. Learning the bull from the bull itself should beat learning it from the goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! We learn a thing from the same thing itself. We do not learn a thing from something outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the 'גופו מגופו' objection, now aimed at the bull's upward count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'itself' means the bull. Its own seven downward sprinklings should set its upward count. Learning from the goat, a different animal, should count less.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive; we learn one law from another
Itself. Here it means the bull's own sprinklings.
The bull of the כהן גדול offered on יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: The words are the same as Step 12, but the target is different. There 'itself' was the goat, and here it is the bull.

phrases.english: On the contrary, we derive a thing from itself,
phrases.notes: Learn the bull's upward count from the bull's own downward count.

phrases.english: and we do not derive a thing from an outside thing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the tie-breaker from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 17's choice of 'upward from upward', which gives the bull one upward sprinkling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparing within the same animal is closer than comparing to another animal, so the bull should get seven upward.

steps.title: All actions equal: seven downward and one upward for both
steps.stepSummary: The same extra words 'כאשר עשה' decide the matter. The two animals match completely: seven downward for both, and one upward for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall do with its blood as he did.' The verse did not need to say 'as he did.' So why does it say it? To teach that all his actions should be the same. Just as the bull gets seven downward, the goat gets seven downward. And just as the goat gets one upward, the bull gets one upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings back the verse from Step 13 and uses it to close the whole discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All his actions equal' works in both directions. The goat takes the bull's downward count, and the bull takes the goat's upward count. The 'גופו מגופו' argument is set aside, and the final count is one upward and seven downward for each animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall do with its blood (the verse about the goat)
Just as ... so too
The goat offered as a חטאת on יום כיפור
Sprinkling of blood

steps.whatToRemember: On יום כיפור, both the פר and the שעיר get one upward sprinkling and seven downward sprinklings. This comes from the extra words 'כאשר עשה', which make all their actions equal. The goat learns its downward count from the bull, and the bull learns its upward count from the goat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the order of sprinklings in the עבודה of יום כיפור, as the כהן גדול counts 'אחת, אחת ואחת...'.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And he shall do with its blood
as he did,"
for the verse did not need to say "as he did,"
so why does the verse say "as he did"?
So that all his actions should be equal:
just as downward with the bull is seven,
so too downward with the goat is seven.
And just as upward with the goat is one,
so too upward with the bull is one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְעָשָׂה אֶת דָּמוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 with the verse and states the final result for both animals.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural decision using the extra words, applied in both directions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull would get seven upward sprinklings, learned from itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Full equality: the bull gets one upward, like the goat.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the פר and the שעיר get one upward and seven downward sprinklings, because 'כאשר עשה' makes all their actions equal.

steps.title: The counting formula, and רבי מאיר's version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's counting words and brings a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's full count: 'one, one and one, one and two' all the way to 'one and seven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he counted: 'One; one and one; one and two.' רבנן taught in a ברייתא: 'One; one and one; one and two; one and three; one and four; one and five; one and six; one and seven.' These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, which is how the כהן גדול counted out loud while sprinkling. It brings a ברייתא that spells out the full count according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first sprinkling is the single upward one, so it is called just 'one.' After that, each downward sprinkling is counted as 'one and ___.' The 'one' stands for the upward sprinkling, which is said again every time. In רבי מאיר's version the 'one' comes before the running number.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This phrase opens a ברייתא.
'One and one.' This means the first upward sprinkling plus the first downward one.
'The words of רבי מאיר.' It tells us whose opinion this is.

steps.confusionAlert: 'One and one' does not mean two sprinklings at the same moment. The first 'one' is just a reminder of the upward sprinkling that was already done. The second number is the downward sprinkling being done right now.

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] One; one and one; one and two.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that it is about to explain.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One; one and one; one and two;
one and three; one and four;

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת וְחָמֵשׁ, אַחַת וָשֵׁשׁ, אַחַת וָשֶׁבַע,
phrases.english: one and five; one and six; one and seven —
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 19 settled that the bull gets one upward and seven downward sprinklings. Now the גמרא explains how those sprinklings were counted out loud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the count goes: one, one and one, one and two, up to one and seven.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version of the count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives the same count but puts the running number first: 'two and one,' 'three and one,' up to 'seven and one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'One; one and one; two and one; three and one; four and one; five and one; six and one; seven and one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי יהודה's version of the count. It sounds like he disagrees with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of sprinklings is exactly the same in both versions. The only change is word order. רבי יהודה says the running downward number first and then adds 'and one' for the upward sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'רבי יהודה says.' This introduces the second opinion.
'Two and one.' The downward count comes first, and the upward sprinkling is added after it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One; one and one; two and one;
three and one; four and one;

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵשׁ וְאַחַת, שֵׁשׁ וְאַחַת, שֶׁבַע וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: five and one; six and one; seven and one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the same ברייתא. It gives a different word order from רבי מאיר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the count goes: one, one and one, two and one, up to seven and one.

steps.title: No real argument: each followed his local custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה do not truly argue. Each one simply used the counting style of his own place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. This Sage spoke according to the custom of his place, and this Sage spoke according to the custom of his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains away what looks like an argument. Both רבנן agree on the law and only describe the count in the way people talked where they lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the number and order of the sprinklings is the same in both versions, the difference is only in style of speech. In one place people said the small number first, and in the other place they said the big number first. So there is no difference in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they do not disagree.' The גמרא is saying there is no real argument here.
'This master is like his place.' He followed his local way of speaking.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this master [spoke] according to [the custom of] his place,
and this master [spoke] according to [the custom of] his place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This resolves the apparent argument between the two versions in steps 20 and 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the argument by explaining that the difference is only local style of speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You might think רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about how the sprinklings must be counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree on the law. Each one used the way of counting that was normal in his place.

steps.title: Why is the first sprinkling counted with every one?
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions agree that the first upward sprinkling is mentioned together with each later sprinkling. The גמרא asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that the first sprinkling must be counted together with each and every one. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what both versions have in common and asks why it is done that way. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It would seem simpler to count the downward sprinklings as plain 'one, two, three.' Yet both versions keep repeating the 'one' of the upward sprinkling. The גמרא wants to know why this repetition is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Everyone.' Both opinions agree on this point.
'In any case' or 'at least.'
The first sprinkling, which is the single upward one.
'What is the reason?'

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
the first sprinkling needs to be counted
with each and every one.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since both versions agree, the גמרא now asks for the reason behind what they agree on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why must the first upward sprinkling be mentioned together with each of the downward sprinklings?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: so he won't lose count
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a practical reason. Repeating the first sprinkling keeps the כהן גדול from making a mistake in his count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: so that he does not make a mistake in the sprinklings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question with a common-sense reason, which is to avoid a counting error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן גדול counted the downward sprinklings by themselves, he might get mixed up about whether the upward one was already included. Then he could do one sprinkling too many or too few. Saying 'one and ___' every time keeps the two kinds of sprinkling clearly separate.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So that he does not make a mistake.'
Sprinklings of the blood.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
So that he does not err in the sprinklings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first answer to the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The counting method is a practical safeguard against miscounting the sprinklings.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: learned from an extra word in the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the rule comes from the פסוק. The extra word ״יַזֶּה״ teaches that the first sprinkling is joined to each of the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says, 'And before the כפורת he shall sprinkle.' The פסוק did not need to say 'he shall sprinkle.' So why does it say 'he shall sprinkle'? It teaches about the first sprinkling, that it must be counted with each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. He finds a source in the תורה, not just a practical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said 'and he shall sprinkle' for the upward sprinkling. It could have gone straight on to 'and before the כפורת seven times.' Saying ״יַזֶּה״ a second time is extra, so רבי יוחנן reads it as a teaching. The first sprinkling must be counted along with each of the seven. For רבי אלעזר this is a sensible safeguard, but for רבי יוחנן it comes from the פסוק itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק says.' This introduces a source from the תורה.
The cover on top of the ארון.
'He shall sprinkle.'
'Since there is no need for the פסוק to say.' This points out an extra word.
'It teaches about.'

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees on one upward and seven downward sprinklings. The upward 'one' is repeated with every later count. רבי מאיר says 'one and two,' and רבי יהודה says 'two and one,' but this is only local style. The reason for repeating the 'one' is either to avoid miscounting (רבי אלעזר) or the extra word ״יַזֶּה״ in the פסוק (רבי יוחנן).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of two kinds of answers: one gives a practical reason, and the other finds a source in the פסוק. The same counting method shows up again later for the other sprinklings of יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: The verse states:
"And before the Ark-cover he shall sprinkle" (Vayikra 16:14).
Since there is no need for it to say "he shall sprinkle,"
why then does it say "he shall sprinkle"?
It teaches about the first sprinkling

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁצְּרִיכָה מִנְיָן עִם כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: that it must be counted with each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second answer to step 23. It gives a source from the פסוק instead of רבי אלעזר's practical reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word ״יַזֶּה״ in ויקרא טז:יד teaches that the first sprinkling is counted together with each of the following ones.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי אלעזר's reason and רבי יוחנן's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just heard two reasons for joining the first sprinkling to each later one. Now it asks whether these two reasons ever lead to a different result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר gave a practical reason, so the count does not get mixed up. רבי יוחנן gave a reason from the פסוק. The גמרא wants a real case where the two reasons would give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: A standard question asking for the practical outcome of two different reasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 24 and 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the reasons of רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן lead to different results.

steps.title: The difference is when he did not count and did not make a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when the כהן גדול did not count the first sprinkling with the others and still did not get confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them in a case where he did not count, and did not make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the difference is a case where the כהן גדול did not repeat the first sprinkling in his count, but he still sprinkled the right number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, counting the first one is only a tool to avoid mistakes. If no mistake happened, nothing is missing. For רבי יוחנן, the פסוק itself requires joining the first sprinkling, so leaving it out of the count is not the proper way, even if the number came out right.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
He counted
He made a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: A 'tool' reason (avoid mistakes) and a 'פסוק' reason (it is required) look the same most of the time. They split only when the tool was not used but no mistake happened.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern in גמרא: when one reason is practical and the other comes from a פסוק, the practical difference is a case where the practical worry did not happen.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he did not count, and did not err.
phrases.notes: He did not count the first sprinkling along with the others, but still got the number right.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּלֹא מָנָה וְלֹא טָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When he did not count and did not err: fine according to רבי אלעזר, but not the proper way according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: he placed the blood on the golden stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה: the כהן גדול went out and set the bowl down on the golden stand in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out and placed it on the golden stand that was in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next words of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the כהן גדול leaves the קודש הקדשים with the leftover blood of the bull and puts it on a golden stand. The ת״ק says there were two stands, one for the bull's blood and one for the goat's blood. רבי יהודה says there was only one, and that is what the גמרא is about to explore.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden stand or pedestal
The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: He went out and placed it
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול leaves the קודש הקדשים with the bowl of the bull's blood.

phrases.english: on the golden stand that was in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא וְהִנִּיחוֹ עַל כַּן הַזָּהָב שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול places the bull's blood on the golden stand in the היכל (with the dispute about how many stands there were).

steps.title: A related source: רבי יהודה says there were no boxes for obligatory bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from שקלים in which רבי יהודה says there were no collection boxes for obligatory bird offerings, because of mix-ups.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there (in שקלים): רבי יהודה says: there were no collection boxes for obligatory bird offerings, because of mix-ups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in another משנה where רבי יהודה shows the same concern about things getting mixed up. This is a setup: the גמרא will explore what this means, to help explain why רבי יהודה said there was only one stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש there were 13 horn-shaped boxes (שופרות) for collecting money for different offerings. רבי יהודה says there was no box for קיני חובה, birds a person is required to bring, because of 'mix-ups'. The גמרא does not yet know what mix-up he means, so the next step asks.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Horn-shaped collection boxes in the מקדש
Obligatory pairs of birds (one חטאת, one עולה)
Mix-ups or mixtures

steps.confusionAlert: 'שופרות' here are not shofars for blowing. They are horn-shaped boxes, narrow at the top, used to collect money.

phrases.english: We learned there:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
There were no collection horns for obligatory bird-pairs,
because of mix-ups.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source showing רבי יהודה's concern about mix-ups, connected to his view of one stand in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, there were no collection boxes for קיני חובה because of תערובות.

steps.title: What mix-up does רבי יהודה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'because of mix-ups' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'because of mix-ups' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which mix-up רבי יהודה was worried about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'mix-ups' is vague. Money could be confused in more than one way, so the גמרא wants to know exactly which mix-up made a separate box a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: What is 'because of mix-ups'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the source quoted in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which mix-up רבי יהודה was worried about.

steps.title: רב יוסף: obligatory money might mix with voluntary money
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the worry was that money for obligatory birds would get mixed with money for voluntary birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: because obligatory money might get mixed with voluntary money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. The fear is that money for required bird offerings will get mixed up with money for voluntary bird offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיני חובה are brought as one חטאת and one עולה. Voluntary birds (נדבה) are both עולות. If the money gets mixed, the birds may be brought the wrong way, and the offerings become invalid. That is why, says רב יוסף, there was no box for obligatory birds.

keyTerms.meaning: An obligatory offering
A voluntary (freewill) offering

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
because of a mix-up of obligatory with voluntary.
phrases.notes: Money for required birds mixing with money for voluntary birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף מִפְּנֵי תַּעֲרוֹבֶת חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mix-up means obligatory money getting mixed with voluntary money.

steps.title: אביי: just make two boxes and label them
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: if that is the worry, make two boxes and write on each one whether it is for obligatory or voluntary birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: let us make two boxes and write on them which one is for obligatory and which one is for voluntary.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's explanation. He says the problem has an easy fix: two labeled boxes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only danger is mixing obligatory money with voluntary money, labels should be enough to keep them apart. So why cancel the obligatory box completely? אביי's question suggests the worry must be something labels cannot fix.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us make
Two
And let us write
Which one

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
So let us make two (boxes)
and write on them
